# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_016_page_001.jpg

---

**16:1** On account of these things they were fittingly punished through similar creatures, and were tormented by a swarm of beasts.

**16:2** Instead of which punishment you benefited your people, and preparing for their craving a delicacy of taste, you provided quails for their appetite.

**16:3** So that those, desiring food, because of the loathsome creatures produced among them, might even turn away from necessary appetite; but these, after a brief want, even partook of a delicacy of food.

**16:4** For it was necessary that inescapable want should come upon those who were acting tyrannically; but to these it was only shown how their enemies were being tormented.

**16:5** For when the fierce rage of wild beasts came upon them and they were perishing by the bites of crooked serpents, your wrath did not continue to the end.

**16:6** But as a warning they were troubled for a short time, having a sign of salvation to remind them of the commandment of your law.

**16:7** For the one who turned to it was saved, not through what was seen, but through you, the Savior of all.

**16:8** And by this also you persuaded our enemies that you are the one who delivers from every evil.

**16:9** For they were killed by the bites of locusts and flies, and no remedy was found to save their life, because they were worthy to be punished by such things.

**16:10** But not even the teeth of venomous serpents overcame your sons; for your mercy came to help and healed them.

**16:11** For they were bitten to recall your oracles, and were quickly saved, lest falling into deep forgetfulness they should become unable to use your kindness.

**16:12** For neither herb nor poultice healed them, but your word, O Lord, which heals all things.

**16:13** For you have authority over life and death, and you lead down to the gates of Hades and bring up again.

**16:14** But a man kills through his wickedness, and when the spirit has gone forth it does not return, nor does he bring back the soul that has been taken.

**16:15** But it is not possible to escape your hand.

**16:16** For the ungodly, refusing to know you, were scourged by the strength of your arm, pursued by unusual rains and hailstorms and unceasing showers, and completely consumed by fire.

**16:17** For, most extraordinary of all, in the water that quenches all things, fire worked more powerfully; for the world is the champion of the righteous.

**16:18** For at one time the flame was gentled so that it should not consume the creatures sent against the ungodly, but so that they, seeing this, might know that they were being pursued by the judgment of God;

**16:19** and at another time even in the midst of water it burned above the power of fire, so that it might destroy the produce of an unrighteous land.

**16:20** Instead of these things you fed your people with food of angels, and without their labor you supplied them from heaven bread ready to eat, giving all delight and suited to every taste.

**16:21** For your sustenance demonstrated your sweetness toward your children, and serving the desire of the one who received it, it was changed to whatever anyone wished.

**16:22** But snow and ice endured fire without melting, so that they might know that fire was destroying the crops of the enemies, burning in the hail and flashing in the showers of rain.

**16:23** But fire again forgot its own power so that the righteous might be nourished.

**16:24** For creation, serving you who made it, exerts itself for punishment against the unrighteous, and slackens for benefit toward those who trust in you.

**16:25** Therefore at that time also, transforming itself into all things, it was obedient to your grace which nourishes all things, according to the will of those who were in want,

**16:26** so that your children whom you loved, O Lord, might learn that it is not the production of crops that nourishes man, but that it is your word that preserves those who trust in you.

**16:27** For what was not destroyed by fire melted away when it was merely warmed by a brief ray of sun,

**16:28** so that it might be known that one must hasten before the sun to give thanks to you and meet you at the first light of day.

**16:29** For the hope of the ungrateful will melt like winter frost and run off like useless water.
